\section[(dialogue)]{The body, health and people — a first pass}

\label{lesson:LA-R85-first-pass-the-body-health-and-people}



\begin{quote}
Say the words for a crown and a ring.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item an arm, a finger, a tooth, the tongue; a language, the nose
  \item the neck, the shoulder, a knee, the heart, blood
  \item a hair, the belly, the back, the forehead, a beard
  \item the chest, a leg, a cheek, a fingernail, healthy
  \item a fever, a cough, pain, medicine, an illness
  \item sick, tired, hunger, thirst, care
  \item joy, anger, fear, happy, sad
  \item a son, a daughter, a grandfather, a grandmother, a family
  \item a husband, a wife, children, a baby, an uncle
  \item an aunt, a neighbour, a guest; a host, a man, a woman
  \item a girl, an old man, a queen, a sailor, a poet
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
An arm? (\textbf{bracchium, bracchiī}.) A finger? (\textbf{digitus, digitī}.) A tooth? (\textbf{dēns, dentis}.) The tongue; a language? (\textbf{lingua, linguae}.) The nose? (\textbf{nāsus, nāsī}.) The neck? (\textbf{collum, collī}.) The shoulder? (\textbf{umerus, umerī}.) A knee? (\textbf{genū, genūs}.) The heart? (\textbf{cor, cordis}.) Blood? (\textbf{sanguis, sanguinis}.) A hair? (\textbf{capillus, capillī}.) The belly? (\textbf{venter, ventris}.) The back? (\textbf{tergum, tergī}.) The forehead? (\textbf{frōns, frontis}.) A beard? (\textbf{barba, barbae}.) The chest? (\textbf{pectus, pectoris}.) A leg? (\textbf{crūs, crūris}.) A cheek? (\textbf{gena, genae}.) A fingernail? (\textbf{unguis, unguis}.) Healthy? (\textbf{sānus, sāna, sānum}.) A fever? (\textbf{febris, febris}.) A cough? (\textbf{tussis, tussis}.) Pain? (\textbf{dolor, dolōris}.) Medicine? (\textbf{medicīna, medicīnae}.) An illness? (\textbf{morbus, morbī}.) Sick? (\textbf{aeger, aegra, aegrum}.) Tired? (\textbf{fessus, fessa, fessum}.) Hunger? (\textbf{famēs, famis}.) Thirst? (\textbf{sitis, sitis}.) Care? (\textbf{cūra, cūrae}.) Joy? (\textbf{gaudium, gaudiī}.) Anger? (\textbf{īra, īrae}.) Fear? (\textbf{timor, timōris}.) Happy? (\textbf{laetus, laeta, laetum}.) Sad? (\textbf{trīstis, trīste}.) A son? (\textbf{fīlius, fīliī}.) A daughter? (\textbf{fīlia, fīliae}.) A grandfather? (\textbf{avus, avī}.) A grandmother? (\textbf{avia, aviae}.) A family? (\textbf{familia, familiae}.) A husband? (\textbf{marītus, marītī}.) A wife? (\textbf{uxor, uxōris}.) Children? (\textbf{līberī, līberōrum}.) A baby? (\textbf{īnfāns, īnfantis}.) An uncle? (\textbf{patruus, patruī}.) An aunt? (\textbf{amita, amitae}.) A neighbour? (\textbf{vīcīnus, vīcīnī}.) A guest; a host? (\textbf{hospes, hospitis}.) A man? (\textbf{vir, virī}.) A woman? (\textbf{fēmina, fēminae}.) A girl? (\textbf{puella, puellae}.) An old man? (\textbf{senex, senis}.) A queen? (\textbf{rēgīna, rēgīnae}.) A sailor? (\textbf{nauta, nautae}.) A poet? (\textbf{poēta, poētae}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Verbs, food, the house and things — a second pass}

\label{lesson:LA-R85-second-pass-verbs-food-the-house-and-things}



\begin{quote}
Say the words for a citizen and a cook.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a citizen, a cook, a merchant, a farmer, a field
  \item to work, to sing, to dance, to laugh, to weep
  \item to wash, to cook, to sell, to swim, to call
  \item to send, to stay, to fall, to put, to find
  \item to live, to enter, to go back, to fear, to rejoice
  \item food, dinner, lunch, breakfast, meat
  \item cheese, oil, a grape, vegetables, an olive
  \item grain, flour, a pear, a fig, a nut
  \item a table, a chair, a bed, a window, a bedroom
  \item a kitchen, a roof, a lamp, a cup, a knife
  \item a chest, paper, a stylus, a writing tablet, a mirror
  \item a ball, a wheel, a sword, a crown, a ring
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A citizen? (\textbf{cīvis, cīvis}.) A cook? (\textbf{coquus, coquī}.) A merchant? (\textbf{mercātor, mercātōris}.) A farmer? (\textbf{agricola, agricolae}.) A field? (\textbf{ager, agrī}.) To work? (\textbf{labōrō, labōrāre}.) To sing? (\textbf{canō, canere}.) To dance? (\textbf{saltō, saltāre}.) To laugh? (\textbf{rīdeō, rīdēre}.) To weep? (\textbf{fleō, flēre}.) To wash? (\textbf{lavō, lavāre}.) To cook? (\textbf{coquō, coquere}.) To sell? (\textbf{vendō, vendere}.) To swim? (\textbf{natō, natāre}.) To call? (\textbf{vocō, vocāre}.) To send? (\textbf{mittō, mittere}.) To stay? (\textbf{maneō, manēre}.) To fall? (\textbf{cadō, cadere}.) To put? (\textbf{pōnō, pōnere}.) To find? (\textbf{inveniō, invenīre}.) To live? (\textbf{vīvō, vīvere}.) To enter? (\textbf{intrō, intrāre}.) To go back? (\textbf{redeō, redīre}.) To fear? (\textbf{timeō, timēre}.) To rejoice? (\textbf{gaudeō, gaudēre}.) Food? (\textbf{cibus, cibī}.) Dinner? (\textbf{cēna, cēnae}.) Lunch? (\textbf{prandium, prandiī}.) Breakfast? (\textbf{ientāculum, ientāculī}.) Meat? (\textbf{carō, carnis}.) Cheese? (\textbf{cāseus, cāseī}.) Oil? (\textbf{oleum, oleī}.) A grape? (\textbf{ūva, ūvae}.) Vegetables? (\textbf{holus, holeris}.) An olive? (\textbf{olīva, olīvae}.) Grain? (\textbf{frūmentum, frūmentī}.) Flour? (\textbf{farīna, farīnae}.) A pear? (\textbf{pirum, pirī}.) A fig? (\textbf{fīcus, fīcī}.) A nut? (\textbf{nux, nucis}.) A table? (\textbf{mēnsa, mēnsae}.) A chair? (\textbf{sella, sellae}.) A bed? (\textbf{lectus, lectī}.) A window? (\textbf{fenestra, fenestrae}.) A bedroom? (\textbf{cubiculum, cubiculī}.) A kitchen? (\textbf{culīna, culīnae}.) A roof? (\textbf{tēctum, tēctī}.) A lamp? (\textbf{lucerna, lucernae}.) A cup? (\textbf{pōculum, pōculī}.) A knife? (\textbf{culter, cultrī}.) A chest? (\textbf{arca, arcae}.) Paper? (\textbf{charta, chartae}.) A stylus? (\textbf{stilus, stilī}.) A writing tablet? (\textbf{tabula, tabulae}.) A mirror? (\textbf{speculum, speculī}.) A ball? (\textbf{pila, pilae}.) A wheel? (\textbf{rota, rotae}.) A sword? (\textbf{gladius, gladiī}.) A crown? (\textbf{corōna, corōnae}.) A ring? (\textbf{ānulus, ānulī}.)
